office_does: One of 98 Washington State Representatives, serving two-year terms writing state law and the state budget for the 34th District (West Seattle, Vashon Island, White Center and part of Burien).
race_blurb: House Majority Leader Joe Fitzgibbon, a 16-year incumbent with a climate and tax record, faces first-time candidate Mary Anito, an operations engineer running on fiscal responsibility combined with public investment; both prefer the Democratic Party. Fitzgibbon took 74.5% in the primary.

candidates.summary: State Representative since 2010 and House Majority Leader since 2022; led passage of the Climate Commitment Act and Clean Fuel Standard and championed the 2026 millionaires' tax.
highlights: Voted for ESSB 6346, the 2026 9.9% tax on income over $1 million, and publicly opposes I-645, which would repeal it [S7][S9]
Led passage of the Climate Commitment Act and Clean Fuel Standard; pledges to protect and strengthen the CCA [S1][S3]
Co-sponsored HB 1296 (2025), the parental-rights amendments that I-1 would undo [S5][S6]

taxes.basis: Voted for and says he led passage of the millionaires' tax, and publicly opposes I-645's repeal of it.

spending.basis: Cites secured investments in education, healthcare and transit and warns repeal would force 'devastating cuts to education'; also credits himself with stabilizing the budget.

climate.basis: Led passage of the Climate Commitment Act and Clean Fuel Standard and pledges to protect and strengthen the CCA.

housing.basis: Voted for the 2025 rent-increase limit and pledges renter and anti-displacement protections, alongside support for building more housing near transit.

experience.basis: Sixteen-year incumbent and House Majority Leader with an enacted climate and tax record.

social.basis: Campaign site commits to protecting reproductive freedom and healthcare access; no documented position on gender-identity issues.

parental-rights.basis: Co-sponsored and voted for ESHB 1296, which replaced I-2081's curriculum-examination right and eliminated some medical-service notifications in favor of student-privacy provisions.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate and operations engineer (REI, Wayfair, Caterpillar) and small-business owner, running on fiscal responsibility alongside public investment in schools and healthcare.
highlights: Argues 'fiscal responsibility and strong public investment are not mutually exclusive' [S1]
Supports fully funding schools and fixing the levy and equalization structure [S3]
Supports universal-healthcare efforts such as the Washington Health Trust and restoring abortion-access funding [S3]

spending.basis: Explicitly pairs budget balancing and 'fiscal responsibility' with fully funding schools, infrastructure and healthcare.

experience.basis: First-time candidate with a private-sector operations background challenging a 16-year incumbent leader.

healthcare.basis: Supports 'efforts toward universal healthcare, such as The Washington Health Trust' while also emphasizing restoring Medicaid funding.

social.basis: Pledges access to reproductive healthcare including restoring funding for abortion access; no documented position on gender-identity issues.
